old: yielded to him in a thrice-plowed fallow field
new: yielded to him in a plowed field
reason: "Thrice-plowed fallow field" is a literal, obscure agricultural detail (ritual triple-plowing) that a general listener has no context for; it reads as odd and distracting rather than as the intended discreet euphemism, though the surrounding sentence (Zeus's jealousy, Iasion's death) still makes sense without it.

old: as children rejoice when their dear father begins to get better after having borne sore affliction for a long time, sent him by some angry spirit, but the gods deliver him from evil, so was Odysseus thankful
new: as children rejoice when a father struck down by some angry spirit's long affliction is finally delivered from it by the gods, so was Odysseus thankful
reason: The dangling participial clause "sent him by some angry spirit" lands three clauses after its subject ("affliction"), so on a first listen it's unclear whether the spirit sent the father, the affliction, or something else; the simile has to be replayed to be understood, which breaks comprehension in audio.

old: cling to the knees of your riverhood
new: cling to your knees, river god
reason: "Riverhood" is not a real English word (unlike "godhood" or "knighthood", there is no established sense of "-hood" attached to "river"); a listener has no way to parse it and it will register as a mistake rather than a coinage, stopping comprehension of Odysseus's prayer mid-line.

old: She also gave him a sharp adze
new: She also gave him a sharp hand axe for shaping wood
reason: "Adze" is an obscure tool name (and an unusual spelling/sound) most general listeners won't recognize; the raft-building narrative continues to make sense without knowing exactly what it is, but the word itself is a stumble.
